scope: Proposition A.1 (Optimality of the lifetime exponent) of the manuscript “Variance of the Random k-SAT Hitting Time” (preprints/Variance-of-the-Random-k-SAT-Hitting-Time-September-27-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 235 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e47a7c16a835f91), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer k ≥ 3, and put β = k/(k − 1). For every real γ < β and all constants D, A > 0, there exist arbitrarily large integers u ≥ k and nonempty sets S ⊆ {0, 1}u such that q1(S) ≥ Au−(k−1) , τk(S) > Dq1(S)−γ . Consequently, the killing-probability exponent β in Proposition 2.3 cannot be decreased in a bound uniform over arbitrary assignment sets, even above any fixed multiple of the scale u−(k−1).
